rationale:
I found no adequacy gap for `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineItem`.

The obligations are assessed against two tests marked as testing the subject. The `Span`, `name_span` and `attachments` requirements are cited context, so I did not reassess them.

**Constructor defaults and field preservation** (`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]`)
- After `OutlineItem::new`, the test asserts `name_span == None`, `attachments.is_empty()`, and `header_span` and `trailer_span` both `None`.
- After `with_header_span`, `with_trailer_span` and `with_name_span`, it asserts the header and trailer spans and the name span.
- It clones an `Outline` containing the item. It then asserts `selector`, `kind`, `span` and `structural_hash` against the values given to `new`.
- These assertions are on the clone, so they also exercise `Clone` for `OutlineItem`.

**`with_attachments` sets the list** (same test)
- It calls `with_attachments` twice, first with a `Comment` and then with an `Annotation`.
- It then asserts that exactly one attachment remains, with kind `Annotation` and span `(4,6)`. A merging or appending implementation would fail this, which is the "sets it to the supplied list" obligation.

**`with_own_hash`** (`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]`)
- The `CustomLanguage` outline builds its root item with `with_own_hash`, using a digest that excludes the selected span.
- The structural hash is "a hello z" and the supplied own digest is "a  z". The test asserts `structural_hash() == "a hello z"` and `fingerprint().value == "a  z"`. This confirms the own digest is kept separate from the structural hash and is what the item's fingerprint uses.
- The selected item has no own hash and `structural_hash() == "selected-digest"`. This shows the two cases are distinguished.
- The same test also asserts the `span` of the root outline item.

**Trait implementations and public shape**
- `Debug` is exercised through `format!("{outline:?}")`, which requires `OutlineItem: Debug`, and by the `{cloned:?}` and `{item:?}` panic messages in the same test.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory against rustdoc and checks that the shipping Habeas consumer compiles against the SDK.
- `#[non_exhaustive]` and the private field are declaration-level properties. They have no behavior that the tests could assert beyond what the API test covers.

I see no plausible requirement-violating behavior in the subject's own text that these tests would accept. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

pub fn with_name_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_header_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_trailer_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_own_hash(self, hash: String) -> Self;

`trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
A named item's `name_span` is `Some` with the span to highlight for its name
in the original source snapshot. The highlighted text may differ from the
name in the selector. Use `selector` to address the item. The file root and
anonymous items have `name_span` set to `None`. `OutlineItem::new` starts with
`None`. Language providers use `with_name_span` to set the highlight within

An *attachment* is a source construct that an outline language associates

decorator on a Python method are examples.
